messages:
anna: Heads-up — partner delivered last week and the birthing center billed the anesthesia as out-of-network despite the anesthesiologist being listed on the insurer roster. Member paid $950 at discharge. EOB shows denial for 'provider not contracted.' Anyone seen this?
devon: Ugh. Can you DM the member ID, date of service, anesthesiologist NPI, and upload the EOB screenshot here? Also ask the member if they have a copy of the anesthesiologist's directory listing.
benefits-bot: Please file a network-discrepancy ticket at https://benefits.redwood.example.com/network-discrepancy and attach: 1) EOB PDF, 2) provider NPI/TIN, 3) insurer directory screenshot (if available), 4) receipt of payment. Mark as urgent — inpatient/maternity. Typical turnaround 5-10 business days; escalate for maternity within 72 hours.
maria-claims: If provider is showing in-network on the insurer side, we can request re-adjudication and an adjusted EOB. If insurer claims anesthesiologist was a different taxonomy or billed under a different NPI, we might need the birthing center to resubmit under the correct billing NPI.
lena-caseworker: Process note — after filing the ticket, please email people-ops@redwood.com with subject "URGENT: maternity anesthesia claim Member 4XXXXX" so we create a manual case and assign me. I'll chase provider relations and the hospital billing office.
birthing-center-bill: Hi all — we can resubmit claim under group NPI if insurer prefers that. We can also produce a signed attestation that the attending anesthesiologist provided services and is affiliated with our center on the DOS. If you want, I can pull our billing detail and send it to you.
anna: Sending DM with member ID and EOB now. The anesthesiologist NPI is listed on insurer search but that page shows a different clinic affiliation.
devon: Two parallel actions: 1) open the discrepancy ticket + manual case, 2) request reprocessing and attach the clinic attestation. If insurer still denies, file an appeal citing incorrect provider linkage and request reimbursement to member.
maria-claims: Also request a pre-determination for future deliveries if member is still pregnant — to avoid repeat OOP. For this DOS we can request retroactive correction.
lena-caseworker: Case created: MAT-2026-311. Assigned to lena-caseworker. I'll email the hospital billing contact and provider relations. Expect initial ack in 48 hrs.
birthing-center-bill: I've emailed our billing extract and attestation to people-ops; we can also re-bill under group NPI if needed — please confirm preferred billing NPI.
anna: Quick template for provider relations (paste fields):

```
To: providerrelations@insurer.example.com
Subject: Request for re-adjudication  Member 4XXXXX  DOS [YYYY-MM-DD]
Body:
Member: [name], DOB: [MM/DD/YYYY], Member ID: 4XXXXX
Provider: [Anesthesiologist name], NPI: [#####]
Facility: [Birthing Center name], Tax ID: [#####]
Attachments: EOB, hospital attestation, provider directory screenshot
Request: reprocess claim as in-network; if system mismatch, please advise correct billing NPI to accept claim. Member paid $950 at discharge; request reimbursement if re-adjudicated.
```

anna: If insurer doesn't respond in 48 hrs, escalate to provider relations manager and include state DOI contact if needed.
devon: One last Q — will HSA/FSA cover the $950 while this is pending?
benefits-bot: Yes — out-of-pocket for eligible medical services can be reimbursed via HSA/FSA with receipts and EOB. If insurer later reimburses the member, they should return funds or adjust.
anna: Thanks everyone — will post updates once insurer replies. :pray:
lena-caseworker: Update 1855556900  insurer acknowledged receipt and opened a claims re-adjudication. ETA 7 business days. I'll post payment/reversal details when available.
